methods: Construct and independently check one source-bound instance of the stated first experiment.

original_card.acceptance_gate: A source-bound arbitrary-input identity and legal producer/consumer boundary with the complete paid and productive target invoice, including restoration, ownership, native alignment and extra charges. Price under the actual current model; historical ceiling.py assumptions must be established before use. A favorable optimistic relaxation keeps a route open but is not a completed supplier. A scoped local result remains useful; expansion requires the family-level budget gate.

actual_scope: On the pinned round-three centre word, the raise-and-lower of all 112 rank-8 Y exit charts through the unique rank-9 frame adds 224 rank-1 children. Deleting any submultiset of the eight rank-8 centre transports saves at most 64 rank mass, so the paid moment rises by at least 160 for every exponent in (0, 1]. Helper targets stay fixed. No new kappa.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for one changed itinerary and says to stop when its optimistic budget fails. This prices the Y-exit round trip named by discussion 1166 comment 19133861, on the #4610 round-three word. It is not another seed of the #5698 binary coframe class, and it does not reopen the closed four-contact chart census or reprice the selected #6030 word.
bottleneck_link: A favourable complex itinerary has to clear a complete signed bill. This route spends 224 rank-1 children to buy at most the whole rank-8 centre budget, so the optimistic paid moment fails before helper-target or caller charges. It does not move the selected exponent.
stop_rule: Stop when the added rank-1 bill exceeds every deletion inside the eight rank-8 centre transports. Do not search the #5698 binary coframe class again, and do not extend the closed four-contact chart census.
evidence: python3 -B research/y-exit-rank-lift-obstruction/verify.py prints PASS_Y_EXIT_RANK_LIFT_OBSTRUCTION with moment_gap_at_least=160. PROOF.md records the width law and the rank-mass comparison.

open_questions.question: Can a route that moves only some Y exits, or that also deletes helper calls, clear a positive paid moment while restoring every rank-8 Y exit?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The all-Y round trip cannot, because 224 already exceeds the rank-8 budget of 64. A cheaper route would be a different itinerary.
open_questions.first_step: Write one literal route whose added rank mass is at most 64, with these exit charts and the 408 helper targets fixed, then recompute the paid histogram.
open_questions.blocked_by: No such route is supplied here. This note only prices the all-Y round trip.

open_questions.question: Can the one-way move of every Y exit onto frame 1 be accepted as an endpoint?
open_questions.why_it_matters: That move still leaves a gap of at least 48, but it replaces each rank-8 Y exit by the rank-9 frame, so the restored-exit tariff does not apply.
open_questions.first_step: Compare one Y role's exit chart before and after the one-way transport and state whether the retained endpoint allows frame 1.
open_questions.blocked_by: The retained endpoint uses the rank-8 Y charts. Accepting frame 1 is a changed endpoint contract, not a consequence of this gap.
